cells.tense: The pull toward what you actually want is running clean, and you can feel it in the present.
cells.act: draw the shape of it without the details
cells.ask: Once this week, put the shape of it on a single page — no dates, no numbers, just the pattern. Keep the page.
cells.core:
What you're drawn toward is doing its job. You steer by it, and because you keep adjusting as you go — a little more here, less there — the pull stays bright instead of burning out. That's the difference between aiming at something and being dragged by it: you're still the one tuning.

The reason that's worth saying is what it's made of. The shine isn't borrowed from a mood or a good week; it's coming from something you built and kept building. When you want to know what it actually is — as opposed to how it feels on a given day — draw the shape of it once, on one page, without the details. The shape is what you keep.

cells.verb: steering toward a light you can only navigate by
cells.place: in the live adjusting of the present, sensing what to add and what to take away

cells.tense: The light has been pushed out in front of you into a future you keep arranging in advance.
cells.act: wait until you know which part matters, then begin with that part
cells.ask: Hold off on the next move until a single piece plainly matters. Start there and leave the rest of the plan untouched.
cells.core:
You can't stop reaching forward. Tomorrow's version of this thing is already lit in your head — how it lands, what it becomes — and you keep tuning the version instead of the thing. The adjusting that usually keeps you level has swung out past what's here, and the brightness has stopped showing you anything. It's shine, not light.

What cuts through is smaller than a plan. Before the next move, hold. Not for certainty — for the one piece that plainly matters now, the one that would go first if you could only do one. Begin with that and leave the rest unsettled. Light that arrives before the work does is the thing to watch for.

cells.tense: The pull that used to point somewhere has gone quiet, left at a door that closed behind you.
cells.act: tend it small and ask nothing of it
cells.ask: Keep one small piece of this alive all week — ten minutes, no goals, nothing asked of it. Skip a day and pick it back up.
cells.core:
You kept at it and it didn't come up. The thing you were steering by is still named somewhere in you, but it stopped showing direction a while back, and the hoping has worn thin. What's left is the shape of the effort without the pull in it.

Go smaller than that. Pick one piece of this — the smallest one that still counts as it — and keep it for a week at a size that asks nothing back. Ten minutes. No progress, no sign you're looking for it. Tending something young means you don't judge it yet and you don't force it. The pull returns on a clock you don't set, and it returns to whatever is still there.

cells.tense: The light is showing through you and you haven't said the switch is yours.
cells.act: keep it at its real size when you are asked to shrink it
cells.ask: When someone asks what you're doing this for, don't downplay it. Say what it is and how far along it is, then stop there.
cells.core:
Something has come through in this — people catch it before you speak of it. They ask what you're building toward and you say it's a side interest, a habit, still messing around with it. Meanwhile the thing is radiating out of you at a steady temperature, and the way you describe it leaves that out.

You are the one with your hands on it, and what you do with it is real. When the question comes, keep the size of it: say what it is, say how far along it is, then stop. No explaining the method. If it comes up twice, hold it twice. A thing kept at its true size doesn't need a speech, and you are the one who keeps it.
